name: Airlines
tagline: Load factor and CASK determine survival.
howItWorks: An airline flies a fixed number of seats whether they sell or not, so an empty seat is revenue gone forever the moment the door closes. The business is a knife-edge between how full the planes are and the cost of flying each seat one kilometre. Fuel is a third to a half of costs and moves with crude, which the airline cannot control, so the only durable edge is a structurally lower cost per seat. That is the entire IndiGo story. Debt and unhedged fuel are what bankrupt the rest.

metrics.why: Seats filled over seats available. Above 85% is efficient; below 80% means yield dilution.
Revenue per available seat kilometre, the pricing-power metric.
Cost per seat kilometre. Lower CASK is a structural cost advantage, IndiGo's moat.
Typically 35-45% of revenue. When crude moves, margins move. Unhedged means high volatility.
Hours flown per aircraft per day. Higher means more revenue from the same fixed asset base.
Revenue per passenger kilometre, a pricing-power indicator. The RASK-yield gap shows ancillary revenue quality.
